body: Are you using the `source_color` hint in your shader? If you use it, the shader should automatically switch between linear and sRGB for you

`source_color` can be used to convert an srgb texture to linear, that is the first of the two workarounds I suggested.
It isn't ideal since I want my raw data to be linear, since that is required for the maths being done to make the procedural textures.

But I also want to point out that although there are potential workarounds here I am looking more at this from the perspective of the other Texture2D classes that can handle this (such as a PNG that becomes a CompressedTexture2D, or a ImageTexture when using a I8 texture).
For those resource types the same texture resource can be used in 2D or 3D with no changes to the default materials.
Those resources types are always stored in sRGB and the default materials use `source_color` if you do the same, then you also won't have to make any modifications.

I see what you are saying, but I still think it's missing a part of it, since what you are suggesting doesn't explain how my Texture2DRD looks different in 2D than it does in 3D (while a ImageTexture can be set up to not do so). 

See the information in my original post, I think this has something to do with the rd_format_srgb member on the RD::TextureStorage::texture.
An ImageTexture set to use certain image formats will behave the same way (e.g. when using RGBA8 it works, but with RGBAF it doesn't).
There clearly exists in the code some method to provide a SRGB view for linear textures, and it isn't accessible for Texture2DRD.

>There clearly exists in the code some method to provide a SRGB view for linear textures, and it isn't accessible for Texture2DRD.

No, I don't think there is such a method. The texture view doesn't actually perform any conversion. In 2d you need to convert it to sRGB, or try 2d hdr.

It may not be the texture view that does the work. But there is something allowing some texture resources to work seamless in both 2D and 3D under the same situation where some textures cannot. 
The cases where it does work requires no manual conversions or any settings to be adjusted.
The screenshots above show that.
I am still digging around the source to find where/how it works so I can see if the same implementation would work for Texture2DRD (it already works for ImageTexture if the associated Image has an i8 format).
Only in 3D or 2D HDR there is a conversion from sRGB -> linear -> sRGB (you can remove `source_color` to skip sRGB -> linear in shader parameters). In 2D it is no conversion (assumed to be sRGB).

Could you upload an MRP to illustrate what the current issue is?
If you want to sample a sRGB texture in GLSL, you can obtain the sRGB view (automatically converted to linear in shader) using `RenderingServer.texture_get_rd_texture(tex, true)`

I can take a look at an MRP but currently this is all tangled up in a bigger project. 
I will test out the method you are recommending, I'm not sure if it will work in this instance since I didn't think that the srgb view was being initiated correctly for rd textures.
I have create a PR here for the changes to be reviewed: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/109004

@DDarby-Lewis  Let's disscuss in this issue.
See https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/109030#issuecomment-3124681233 😅, so I think this doesn't need to be fixed. Can you confirm that using `R8G8B8A8_SRGB` works for you? See also #106515 to avoid errors when creating it.

I have done testing with using the srgb format and found it didn't quite work, but I will take a look at your work and re try my testing.
Note that one issue here is not just if there is a way to get the srgb to work in 2D+3D but also the lack of parity when using rd textures Vs standard 2d textures. Standard 2d textures with the 8 bit formats do work in 2D and 3D since they have the srgb view added correctly, and this simply isn't the case with the rd textures (there is an attempt to add it, but the ordering of the views and the initialisations are such that it simply doesn't work, at least in all my tests).
